problem: MLLM-based VLN agents rely on 2D image-text visual encoders lacking globally consistent 3D reasoning; existing 3D-augmented methods reuse off-the-shelf static geometry models (e.g. VGGT) that degrade in dynamic scenes with moving humans. History-token handling (subsampling, pooling, or voxel pruning requiring simulator GT pose/depth) is lossy, costly or not deployable.
motivation: Real-world navigation happens in dynamic, crowded 3D environments and needs geometry robust to moving people, while long-horizon streaming causes token explosion. A monocular-RGB-only system with self-inferred pose and geometry would simplify real-robot deployment.
key_idea: Build a dynamic geometry foundation model (depth-guided 3D embeddings injected into a pi3-style backbone, trained on a new dynamic human dataset DyHM3D), fuse its tokens with Qwen2-VL visual tokens by cross-attention, and prune historical tokens with a pose-free occupancy-aware voxel strategy using the model's own poses and points.
insight: Both branches matter: removing visual semantics drops HA-VLN val-unseen SR from 0.40 to 0.30, and removing spatial geometry drops it to 0.34. Removing dynamic spatial injection lowers SR to 0.36 and removing token pruning to 0.37, so pruning helps performance and not just efficiency, presumably by discarding redundant tokens. Geometry inferred from monocular RGB suffices to beat panoramic RGB-D/odometry methods on R2R-CE.
method: Dynamic Geometry Foundation Model (DGFM): Depth Anything depth gives a local point map, encoded by a point-map Transformer into multi-level 3D embeddings; these are added to the pi3 backbone's per-layer features via zero-initialized convolutions (ControlNet-style).

Hierarchical latent decoding: shared decoder tokens go to camera and local-point decoders, whose outputs are aggregated to condition a global-point decoder, giving temporally consistent geometry tokens and poses.

DyHM3D dataset: ~50k first-person trajectories with simulated walking humans in HM3D (nav-mesh waypoints, skeletal human models, varied camera heights/FoV) with RGB, depth, pose and intrinsics, used to train DGFM.

Cross-branch 2D-3D fusion: Qwen2-VL visual tokens are queries and aligned DGFM global tokens are keys/values in multi-head cross-attention; the fused tokens go to the LLM with instruction tokens, which outputs discrete actions (Forward/Left/Right/Stop).
Sliding-window KV cache: recent N frames are kept active with a KV cache, while older frames enter as pruned memory tokens (StreamVLN-style), bounding memory and runtime.

Adaptive-resolution occupancy-aware token pruning: tokens are voxelized in world coordinates using self-predicted pose and points, with depth-adaptive voxel size; per voxel, latest/priority/top-K rules select tokens.

Token completion and temporal smoothing: a minimum keep ratio is enforced by re-adding top-importance tokens (feature magnitude, range, spatial distribution, recency), and pruning masks are majority-voted over a 3-frame window.
Real-world variant: the model is paired with a diffusion action head that predicts pixel goals plus a low-level diffusion trajectory module and MPC controller on a Unitree Go1.

setting.backbone: Qwen2-VL (vision encoder + LLM fine-tuned) + DGFM (pi3-initialized geometry model, frozen during VLN training)
setting.training_data: R2R-CE, RxR-CE, EnvDrop, HA-VLN, ScaleVLN, plus DAgger; DGFM trained on DyHM3D (~50k trajectories)
setting.observation: monocular egocentric RGB stream only (poses/point clouds inferred by DGFM)
setting.action_space: low-level discrete: Move Forward / Turn Left / Turn Right / Stop (real robot: diffusion head producing pixel goal and continuous trajectories)

numbers_note: Real-world success rates only appear in a figure (20 episodes per scenario), so they are not extracted. HA-VLN SR and CR are printed as fractions.
results: On R2R-CE val-unseen, DyGeoVLN reaches SR 60.8 / SPL 55.8 / NE 4.41 with monocular RGB, beating StreamVLN (55.7/50.9) and NavFoM (56.2/51.2), and it also exceeds panoramic RGB-D methods such as g3D-LF (61.0 SR is essentially matched, with better OSR/SPL/NE). On dynamic HA-VLN it gets SR 0.44/0.40 (seen/unseen) versus g3D-LF 0.32/0.27 and StreamVLN 0.34/0.33, with lower collision rates.
limitations: Real-world evaluation is small (20 episodes per scenario) and shown only in a figure, with no detailed numbers.
The dynamic dataset covers only simulated humans, and DGFM needs a separate training stage and an external depth estimator, so gains rely on that added pipeline.
Ablations are only on HA-VLN val-unseen, with no efficiency or latency numbers reported for token pruning.
